stem:
The table shows some standard entropy data.

| substance | standard entropy, $S^\ominus$ / $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{PbO}_2\text{(s)}$ | 77 |
| $\text{PbO}\text{(s)}$ | 69 |
| $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ | 205 |

Lead(IV) oxide, $\text{PbO}_2$, decomposes to lead(II) oxide, $\text{PbO}$, and oxygen when heated.

$$2\text{PbO}_2\text{(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{PbO}\text{(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H^\ominus = +118\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use the data to calculate the value of $\Delta S^\ominus$ for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the value of $\Delta H^\ominus$ and your answer to (a) to calculate the temperature at which this reaction becomes feasible.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Solid lead(II) oxide can be made by heating lead metal in air.

Predict the **sign** of the standard entropy change of this reaction. Explain your answer.
